questions.text: A curve of how much attention lands on the image: what can it support, and what can it not?

relations.question: q-attention-share-evidence
relations.purpose: Read why a high attention weight can mean only "the surplus has to land somewhere". The letter under the doors is the reading copy; reading needs no experiment.
relations.reason: The draft already names this gate (DarwinLibrary anchor) as its place; it stays the reading place. The library gate is where Snowdrop leaves things to read, not to run.

relations.label: simulated
relations.question: q-attention-share-evidence
relations.purpose: Run the Attention Fade toy model on the blackboard twice, re-looking at the image never (interval 0) and every 512 tokens, and note what the curve shows and what it leaves open.
relations.limits: Attention Fade is an illustrative toy model, not fitted to any model or paper. A run here does not reproduce StreamingLLM, measures no real VLM, and cannot verify the paper or the reading.
relations.reason: The classroom blackboard already opens Attention Fade (G). It is the place to try the question, separate from where the reading is kept.

relations.question: q-attention-share-evidence
relations.purpose: Bring the two saved runs to Saturnus and hear what they can and cannot support. What she says goes into her case log as one line, next to the reading you file.
relations.limits: Saturnus checks the scope of two toy runs. She has no real model data either; her line is an audit of what the runs can carry, not a result.
relations.reason: Saturnus keeps her cases in the police office case log (the curated shelf there). The route's check belongs with her, apart from the reading and the experiment.
